chunks: Who is it who stands (watch) over every soul for what it does? Yet they ascribe compeers to God. Say: "Then name them. Or are you announcing to God what He does not know on the earth? Or is it only empty talk? In fact, the unbelievers' plots are made to look attractive to them, so that they are held back from the right path. Whosoever God allows to go astray has none to show him the way.
ai.seo_question: What does the Quran say about God's knowledge of every soul and the attribution of partners to Him?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse underscores the concept of divine omniscience (Ilm al-Ghayb) as an exclusive attribute of Allah, refuting the polytheists' claim that their idols share in divine knowledge or power. The rhetorical challenge to 'name them' highlights the absurdity of attributing partners to the All-Knowing, while the concluding phrase emphasizes that misguidance is a consequence of one's own rejection of the truth, a theme central to the Imams' teachings on free will and divine decree.
